### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. autosomal dominant mitochondrial myopathy with exercise intolerance  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.782)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:15559)

**Proposed mechanism:** CHCHD10 (HGNC:24021) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial respiratory chain complex assembly (GO:0005746); Mitochondrial respiratory chain complex assembly (GO:0005746) —LEADS_TO→ Mitochondrial dysfunction (HP:0001250); Mitochondrial respiratory chain complex assembly (GO:0005746) —LEADS_TO→ Myopathy (HP:0003198); Mitochondrial dysfunction (HP:0001250) —LEADS_TO→ Exercise intolerance (HP:0011329); Myopathy (HP:0003198) —LEADS_TO→ Exercise intolerance (HP:0011329). Loss-of-function variants in CHCHD10 disrupt mitochondrial respiratory chain complex assembly, leading to general mitochondrial dysfunction. This mitochondrial dysfunction manifests as exercise intolerance and, in the context of autosomal dominant mitochondrial myopathy, also directly contributes to the development of myopathy.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in CHCHD10 with a consistent gain-of-function mechanism for both diseases would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs1410097718)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of CHCHD10 in these distinct but related mitochondrial disorders could lead to the development of therapies targeting mitochondrial function that benefit patients with both conditions.
